rules.title: Berkeley ban on coordinated pricing algorithms for rents and occupancy
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use, and vendors may not sell or provide, coordinated pricing algorithms that use nonpublic competitor data to set or recommend rents or occupancy levels for Berkeley residential units. The City Attorney or an aggrieved tenant can sue for civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation.
rules.key_value: ban on coordinated pricing algorithms using nonpublic competitor data (<90 days old); civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley
rules.effective_date_note: The ordinance document provided (passed to print Nov 18, 2025) states no effective date; 2026-03-01 is the date reported for the ordinance text. The Morgan Lewis alert says January 2026.
rules.exemptions: Excludes aggregated anonymous reports that do not recommend rents, affordable-housing rent/income limit products, and market research for financing, appraisal, or software development research/testing/training.
rules.penalty: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; damages, injunctive relief, restitution; each month and each unit is a separate violation; prevailing plaintiff gets attorney's fees
rules.conflict_note: Two published effective dates: March 1, 2026 (ordinance text, as reported) vs. January 2026 (August 2026 law-firm alert D002/D037). The provided ordinance document itself does not state a date.

rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Berkeley landlords may not ask about or use criminal history in advertising, applications, tenant selection, or lease decisions, and must give written notice and a chance to respond before taking any action based on criminal history.
rules.key_value: ban on criminal-history inquiries and use in tenant selection
citation_aliases: Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making
rules.effective_date_note: Council passed the ordinance April 14, 2020; the document does not state the effective date.
rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8; owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units where an owner of record lives in one unit; owner move-back rental agreements; existing tenants subletting or adding/replacing roommates.
rules.penalty: Administrative fines of $1,000 to $10,000 per violation, actual damages or three times one month's rent, punitive damages, attorneys' fees and costs, injunctive relief.

unverifiable_exemptions: existing tenants subletting or adding/replacing roommates

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Good Cause Ordinance (just cause, notice and relocation assistance)
rules.requirement: Tenants in fully or partially covered units can be evicted only for just cause. Nonpayment evictions require debt of at least one month of HUD Fair Market Rent, eviction notices must refer tenants to the Rent Board and be filed with it within three business days, and owner move-in and Ellis Act evictions require relocation assistance ($19,413 plus $6,471 for qualifying households in 2026).
rules.key_value: Just cause required; nonpayment only if debt ≥ 1 month HUD FMR; OMI/Ellis relocation $19,413 + $6,471 (2026)
citation_aliases: Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: In Berkeley, tenants in units that are fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance cannot be evicted unless there is
rules.effective_date_note: Measure BB amendments passed in the November 2024 election; no general effective date stated in the documents. Relocation payment adjustment effective 2026-01-01.
rules.exemptions: Exempt: golden duplexes, units sharing kitchen/bath with an owner who lived there first, certain ADU properties, university housing, nonprofit cooperatives.
rules.conflict_note: Chapter number is inferred (ch. 13.76 appears in other Berkeley documents); local just cause governs in place of the state Civ. Code § 1946.2 for covered units.

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Stabilization Ordinance – Annual General Adjustment (max 5%)
rules.requirement: For fully covered (rent-controlled) units, yearly rent increases are limited to the Annual General Adjustment set by the Rent Board, 65% of the Bay Area CPI and never more than 5%. The 2026 AGA is 1.0%, allowed no earlier than January 1, 2026.
rules.quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%. This means that, if the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA that is greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%
rules.effective_date_note: Cap added by Measure BB (Nov 2024 election); no effective date stated. 2026 AGA effective 2026-01-01.
rules.exemptions: Partially covered and exempt units (newer construction, most single-family homes and condos) have no rent ceiling; Costa-Hawkins vacancy decontrol applies.
rules.interaction: Local rent control supersedes the state Tenant Protection Act cap (Civ. Code § 1947.12) for covered units; Costa-Hawkins limits local control of newer buildings and single-family homes/condos.
rules.conflict_note: Documents describe the cutoff as 'built before 1980' (fully covered) and 'Certificate of Occupancy after June 1980' (not rent controlled); exact boundary used here is June 30, 1980. D006 says 'after 1980'.

unverifiable_exemptions: single-family homes and condominiums mostly not rent controlled

rules.title: Berkeley security deposit interest requirement
rules.requirement: For units fully or partially covered by the Berkeley Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on security deposits at the end of each year, prorated if the tenant moves out earlier.
rules.quoted_span: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year
rules.coverage_conditions: Units fully or partially covered by the Berkeley Rent Ordinance (includes newer construction and condos; exempt: golden duplexes, owner-shared kitchen/bath, university housing, nonprofit cooperatives).
rules.interaction: Operates alongside the state deposit cap in Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5.
rules.conflict_note: Code section for interest requirement not stated in documents; ch. 13.76 inferred.

rules.title: Berkeley tenant screening fee disclosure and ban on non-refundable renewal fees
rules.requirement: Owners who charge a screening fee must give applicants a Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement and the state maximum fee cap before taking the fee. Landlords also cannot charge existing tenants non-refundable renewal fees, including roommate-change fees.
rules.key_value: Fee-rights/cap disclosure before fee; no non-refundable renewal fees
rules.quoted_span: the owner must provide, either in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap permitted under
rules.interaction: Fee cap itself comes from Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6 ($68.96 for 2026).

parsed.notes: Merged by law: ch. 13.63 (3 candidates), ch. 13.76 split by category (rent, just cause, deposit interest), ch. 13.78 fees (2 candidates). Rent Board Reg. 1148 folded into the rent ordinance record. Berkeley algorithmic ban effective date conflict (2026-03-01 vs January 2026) noted. Rent control cutoff boundary (1980 vs June 1980) is ambiguous in the documents.
